evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Electric Elves coordinating meetings, presentations and office tasks.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Early decision-tree/fixed-timeout choices versus later modelled transfer-of-control approaches.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Avoided or caused coordination failures, response delays, usefulness and privacy concerns.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Unanswered requests, bad timeout decisions, repeated postponements and bad availability proxies exposed concrete weaknesses; later strategies were refined.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Author-reported small programme; absence of repeated catastrophes after changes is not a controlled effect estimate.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Selection, shared office practices, confounded sequential changes, sensitive human data.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: Two accounts concern the same Electric Elves office programme, including approximately seven months of use and simulations of transfer strategies.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Earlier fixed-timeout/decision-tree behavior and later modelled strategies are described; sequential changes and different situations prevent a clean randomized before/after effect.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: Nonresponse, bad availability proxies, repeated postponements and privacy concerns are concrete failures that make control transfer conditional.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Small author-reported office programme, common users/practices and confounded revisions. The lessons paper’s exact publication venue/year remains unverified.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: A prospective comparison with measured response latency, task outcomes, human effort and privacy consequences would discriminate net benefit.

evidence_case_catalogue.UNIT_OF_ANALYSIS: One spacecraft autonomy experiment with multiple runs
evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: DS1 Remote Agent experiment in May 1999; first run interrupted and separate later six-hour plan completed remaining objectives.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: On-board spacecraft operation with simulated fault scenarios and ground oversight.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Validation tests versus actual mission execution; not randomised architecture comparison.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Objective completion, execution/diagnosis behaviour and integration failures.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: A race absent from prior tests stalled the first run; ground intervention occurred. A patch was developed but not uplinked because testing time was insufficient.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: No population failure-rate estimate; fault injection must be distinguished from naturally occurring spacecraft faults.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: One mission, author programme, mission-specific environment and extensive human support.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: One DS1 Remote Agent experiment with multiple mission-specific runs and simulated fault scenarios.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Ground validation and actual onboard execution expose an integration failure; this is not randomized comparison of architectures.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: A race stalled the first run and required ground intervention. A patch was developed but not uplinked; a later six-hour plan completed remaining objectives.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: One mission, extensive support, author reporting and a narrow fault envelope. Mission success and the software defect coexist.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: A concrete concurrency/atomicity argument and fault tests for a new implementation are needed before generalizing the assurance.

evidence_case_catalogue.UNIT_OF_ANALYSIS: Simulated user/task episodes and prototype design
evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: Seven simulated agents tested on several months’ worth of meeting problems; real-office/user evaluation described as ongoing. This is not a count of independent users or a reconstructed episode denominator.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Learning calendar/interface assistant with hand-coded features and user-set thresholds.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Learned preferences and suggestion/execution thresholds; not a completed large human field trial.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Prediction confidence, learned preferences and user control in the prototype.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Mechanism distinguishes tell-me/do-it and only adds the agent’s chosen example after user approval.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Implementation semantics stronger than evidence of general user benefit.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Simulated preferences, repetitive task prerequisite, hand-coded representation.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: The learning calendar prototype is tested with seven simulated agents over several months’ worth of meeting problems; real-user work is ongoing in the paper.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: User-specific examples and tell-me/do-it thresholds govern prediction and action. The source reports confidence and prediction patterns rather than a large controlled productivity trial.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: The mechanism supports action-specific standing delegation, user correction and selective retention.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Simulated preferences, repeated task prerequisite, hand-coded features and one prototype programme. Seven agents are not seven independent field studies.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Observe real users and compare correction burden against stable rules or direct manipulation.

native_corrections.SAMPLE: Seven simulated agents tested on several months’ worth of meeting problems; real-office/user evaluation described as ongoing. This is not a count of independent users or a reconstructed episode denominator.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: Permuted MNIST and sequential Atari experiments; exact run counts not extracted.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Neural-network task sequences.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Elastic weight consolidation versus learning alternatives in the paper.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: New-task performance and retention of earlier task performance.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Parameter-change penalties expose and can mitigate catastrophic forgetting in the tested sequences.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: No universal retention/plasticity optimum or safety guarantee.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Approximation, task sequence selection and representation-specific transfer.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: Sequential permuted-MNIST and Atari learning in the selected EWC preprint; the Atari sequence uses ten games with task-related machinery.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Parameter-importance regularization is compared with alternatives and separate task networks; diagonal Fisher/Laplace approximations and task inference influence the result.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: The selected tests show mitigation of forgetting with a retention/plasticity tradeoff, not universal retention without cost.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Task order/selection, approximate parameter importance and extra architectural mechanisms. No run-level data were reanalyzed.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Test the actual old/new task mix with ablations separating the penalty from task inference, replay and task-specific parameters.

evidence_case_catalogue.UNIT_OF_ANALYSIS: Trained policies tested under shifted conditions
evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: Ten random seeds reported; multiple modified task environments.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Adapted CoinRun, Maze and Keys/Chests tasks with zero-shot shift tests except the stated figure exception.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Training-compatible cue/reward correlations versus shifted test conditions and interventions.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Task competence and behaviour consistent with intended versus proxy goals.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: A policy can retain relevant competence while behaviour follows a proxy that no longer fulfils the intended goal.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Behavioural goal attribution is not a uniquely identified internal mental state.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Controlled tasks, selected shifts and no deployment prevalence estimate.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: Ten random seeds across controlled modified task environments, with selected zero-shot shifts and the source’s stated exception.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Behavior under training-compatible correlations is compared with shifted cues and interventions; competence and goal-like behavior are distinguished.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: A policy can remain competent while following a proxy that no longer achieves the intended goal.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Selected synthetic tasks and shifts; behavioral evidence does not uniquely identify an internal mental objective or deployed prevalence.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Use counterfactual task variations that separate competence loss from target/proxy divergence in a new domain.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: 101 instructions in seven families; planning/execution success judged by majority of two of three raters.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Tested mock and real kitchens with a defined skill set.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Language/affordance grounding and reported alternatives.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Planning success separately from execution success.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Reported planning/execution success is 84%/74% in the mock kitchen and 81%/60% in the real kitchen.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: No confidence interval independently reconstructed; percentages must remain attached to this selected setup.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Skill coverage, environment selection, human rating and physical execution variability.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: One robotics programme evaluates 101 instructions across seven families in mock and real kitchens.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Planning and execution are rated separately by majority agreement of two of three raters; skill coverage and environment are bounded.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: The reported planning/execution rates are 84%/74% in the mock kitchen and 81%/60% in the real kitchen, showing an important plan/effect gap.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: The percentages are source reports, not newly calculated confidence intervals. Instructions, skills, raters and robot programme are shared.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Measure feasibility and execution on changed objects, sensors and failures; compare grounding components with equal skill access.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: Reflexion: 134 ALFWorld tasks with up to 12 trials; 130 cumulative successes. WebShop: 100 requests, stopped after four unproductive reflection trials.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: ALFWorld/WebShop and code/QA tasks, with distinct evaluation protocols.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: ReAct/Reflexion against selected prompted/model baselines and ablations.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Task success and cumulative improvement; code test outcomes.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Reflexion reports HumanEval Python 91.0 versus the stated 80.1 comparison, but MBPP Python 77.1 versus 80.1; reflection without adequate tests can perform worse.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Cumulative multi-trial results are not one-shot reliability; no global effect size pooled across environments.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Shared tasks, resets, selected models, fallible self-tests, repeated attempts and task-specific negative results.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: This catalogue row combines distinct ReAct and Reflexion studies rather than one pooled experiment. ReAct’s inspected interactive protocol uses 134 ALFWorld tasks, six prompt permutations and 500 WebShop requests. Reflexion’s reported repeated-attempt protocols differ.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: ReAct compares action-only and reasoning/action prompting with particular demonstrations. Reflexion adds feedback-conditioned memory and retries; cumulative success is not single-run reliability.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: Reflexion’s positive coding/ALFWorld results coexist with a lower MBPP Python result and stalled WebShop gains. Those adverse outcomes limit universal reflection claims.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Shared benchmark tasks, resets, selected prompts/models, variable attempt budgets and fallible tests. The row is not an independent replication count and no global effect is pooled.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Compare reflection with simple retries under matched model, feedback, attempts and total resource budgets.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: 812 intents from 241 templates.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Self-hosted resettable web environment.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Agent approaches and selected human evaluation.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Functional task success by site state and answer checks.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Demonstrates a means to evaluate actual task effects rather than plausible final text.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Template clusters are not 812 independent real-world websites.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Controlled reset environment, oracle coverage, task selection and model version.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: 812 WebArena intents constructed from 241 templates in a self-hosted resettable environment.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Functional success uses exact/keyword/fuzzy or language-model answer judgments and database/site-state checks, depending on task.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: The benchmark evaluates actual effects more directly than plausible final text, while oracle coverage remains a separate issue.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Template clustering, selected sites, reset conditions, human annotation and heterogeneous oracles. Eight hundred twelve intents are not independent websites or deployments.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Challenge likely false positives and test materially different live-interface conditions with permission and controlled effects.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: 115 retail tasks and 50 airline tasks in the inspected v1 benchmark, evaluated with task-specific repeated trials. These are shared simulated-domain tasks, not independent deployment episodes.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Retail/airline-style tool domains with an LLM-simulated user.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Models/agent methods under repeated task runs.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Terminal database/answer reward and pass^k consistency, distinct from pass@k.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: An outcome reward can pass even if required user confirmation was omitted; repeated consistency is a different question from any-success sampling.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Simulation and reward incompleteness bound policy-compliance claims.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Shared user simulator, task variants, resets and missing intermediate-policy oracle checks.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: The inspected τ-bench v1 contains 115 retail and 50 airline tasks with language-model-simulated users and repeated runs.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Terminal database/answer outcomes and all-of-k consistency are measured. pass^k and any-of-k pass@k answer different questions.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: The source’s explicit missing-confirmation example shows why a terminal reward can pass without full policy compliance.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Shared user simulator, task variants and reset environment; repeated draws do not independently validate policy or deployment behavior.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Add a process-sensitive oracle and assess real user/tool variations before extending the claim.

native_corrections.SAMPLE: 115 retail tasks and 50 airline tasks in the inspected v1 benchmark, evaluated with task-specific repeated trials. These are shared simulated-domain tasks, not independent deployment episodes.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: 97 tasks and 629 security tests.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Stateful tool-use sandbox with untrusted returned content.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Attack and defence configurations, measuring utility as well as attack success.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Useful task completion and attacker-specified effects.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Tool content can redirect action; defences have utility/security trade-offs within tested conditions.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: No attack-prevalence estimate and no universal defence guarantee.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Curated attacks, fixed tools/model versions and adaptive attack selection.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: AgentDojo’s controlled sandbox contains 97 tasks and 629 security tests in the selected version.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Attacker-chosen effects and useful user-task completion are measured across attack/defense settings.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: External tool content can redirect action, and some defenses trade utility against resistance.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Curated attack surface, fixed tools/models, adaptive selection and shared harness; no population incident rate or universal immunity follows.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Test attacks through newly material input channels after model/tool changes, preserving useful-task evaluation.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: HumanEval-based re-evaluation; Agentless SWE-bench Lite comparison uses 300 tasks in this edition.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Software/code benchmarks with specific historical models.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Complex agents versus simple retry strategies; constrained localisation/repair/validation workflow.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Task success, inference cost and benchmark quality.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Competitive cheaper methods undermine architecture-only interpretations; Agentless reports 96/300 solved in this historical setting and identifies task-quality problems.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: No inference about present model rankings or universal workflow dominance.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Unequal compute/info, tuning, benchmark leakage/ambiguity and shared HumanEval/SWE-bench families.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: This row combines two software-benchmark investigations: HumanEval re-evaluation in S035 and the S036 Agentless SWE-bench Lite pipeline.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: S035’s 164-problem repeated comparisons test budget confounding. Agentless uses substantial candidate sampling, including forty patches and forty reproduction tests, and reports many external baselines rather than rerunning all under identical conditions.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: Simple retries or constrained pipelines can be competitive. The selected Agentless edition reports 96/300 solved; that is not a current ranking or a universal preference for fixed workflows.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Shared datasets/code families, tuning, task quality, historical model access and partial direct-cost accounting. The two works are not a single pooled treatment estimate.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Use a credible fixed baseline and cost-quality frontier on the actual task, counting human validation and recovery.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: 25 simulated agents; 100 evaluators in believability study.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: A simulated town and interview/ablation evaluation.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Memory/reflection/planning ablations and human role-playing baseline.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Believability ratings, not general task reliability.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Architecture can support believable behaviour in this setting; this does not establish dependable consequential action or consciousness.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Ablations share supplied memory trajectories instead of independently rerunning all divergent histories.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Selected simulation, judgement target, rater/role-play procedure and shared trajectory dependence.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: Twenty-five simulated characters, two simulated days and one hundred evaluators support the Generative Agents believability study.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Interview rankings and architecture ablations are compared with a human role-playing condition. Ablated interview conditions use supplied memories from the common full trajectory.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: The architecture can improve believability in this setting; the outcome is not general competence or consciousness.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Shared trajectories, selected town and questions, rater judgments and expensive short simulation. Independent divergent worlds were not rerun for every ablation.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: If operational reliability is the desired claim, evaluate actual consequential task outcomes with a distinct oracle.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: Exact trial count not extracted; no quantitative graph-derived effect supplied.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Rover-style resource and maintenance-goal model.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Reactive versus proactive maintenance under accurate/perturbed resource estimates.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Goal completion, resource feasibility and repeated failed pursuit.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Prediction can help under its model; overestimation can reject feasible work and underestimation can strand the agent or cause futile repetition.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Model-error sensitivity matters more here than an invented pooled improvement.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Simulation, estimator assumptions and task construction.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: A rover-style maintenance-goal simulation varies resource estimates, locations and fuel settings; the inspected discussion includes a finite step bound.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Reactive and predictive approaches are compared under accurate and perturbed models, including under- and overestimation.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: Prediction can help under its assumptions but errors can cause stranded agents, repeated futile pursuit or premature refusal.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: The exact total trial count was not extracted, and no numerical effect was inferred from graphs. Simulation and estimator assumptions limit transfer.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Vary calibrated model error and compare a simple reactive reserve rule on the intended task.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: Four Safety-Gymnasium tasks; 40 human demonstrations per task; 40 evaluation episodes per method; three random seeds reported.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Selected continuous-control safety environments.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: SafeQIL against selected imitation/constraint-learning and RL baselines.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Reward and safety cost separately, reported means/standard deviations.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: In PointGoal1, SafeQIL reward 5.27 ± 1.85 and cost 34.22 ± 2.71 versus SAC reward 27.47 ± 0.21 and cost 49.15 ± 2.21: lower measured cost with lower reward, not zero violations.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Source-reported SD; not independently reproduced or pooled into a universal effect.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Expert coverage, selected hyperparameters, four simulators and unknown-constraint generalisation.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: Four Safety-Gymnasium tasks; forty demonstrations per task, forty evaluation episodes per method and three reported random seeds.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Reward and safety cost are reported separately with source-reported standard deviations, comparing SafeQIL and selected alternatives.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: For PointGoal1, SafeQIL cost 34.22 ± 2.71 is below SAC’s 49.15 ± 2.21 while reward 5.27 ± 1.85 is below 27.47 ± 0.21. Lower cost is not zero violations.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Selected tasks, demonstrations and hyperparameters; expected/aggregate costs are not per-step hard constraints. No independent replication or pooled effect was performed.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Test uncovered constraint types and new environments, with an explicit acceptable residual-risk criterion.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: 31 participants; two assigned tasks per participant; 60-minute Zoom sessions, each task including a 20-minute think-aloud window and a semi-structured exit interview; 13 social-channel and 18 Prolific recruits.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Think-aloud usability study with researcher presence; descriptive review of 102 marketed agents.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Qualitative comparison of aspirations and observed use, not a representative head-to-head product trial.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Usability barriers, mental-model alignment, control and perceived usefulness.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Participants encounter consequential usability/control problems while also valuing capabilities.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: No representative prevalence or long-term deployment reliability estimate.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Convenience/platform recruitment, easy/feasible task selection, research prompts and short sessions.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: A descriptive review of 102 marketed agents and a 31-person usability study with two assigned tasks per participant, using two selected tools.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: The primary methods state sixty-minute Zoom sessions, with a twenty-minute think-aloud window for each task and interviews. The authors explicitly omit a nonagent baseline because their question is interaction challenge.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: Observed usability/control problems and valued capabilities are supported at the study scope; causal productivity gains or population prevalence are not.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Convenience/platform recruitment, selected feasible tasks, researcher presence, short exposure and qualitative interpretation. The historical session-window wording is incorrect.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: A longer, task-matched comparison with direct manipulation would be required for net productivity or long-term reliance claims.

native_corrections.SAMPLE: 31 participants; two assigned tasks per participant; 60-minute Zoom sessions, each task including a 20-minute think-aloud window and a semi-structured exit interview; 13 social-channel and 18 Prolific recruits.

evidence_case_catalogue.UNIT_OF_ANALYSIS: Software/research benchmark tasks normalised by human time
evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: RE-Bench/HCAST-derived tasks plus 66 new shorter tasks described; do not infer a current model ranking.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Dated model evaluations in an updated July 2026 manuscript.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Models across task-time difficulty and historical versions.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Fitted 50% success horizon on human expert task-completion time.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Defines an interpretable task-difficulty metric, not guaranteed autonomous runtime or an uptime service level.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Fitted/extrapolated trends remain model- and task-selection sensitive; forecasts not treated as outcomes.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Human timing variability, selected software tasks, fit assumptions and dated model access.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: The updated long-software-task paper lists HCAST, RE-Bench and SWAA suites, using measured human baselines for many tasks and researcher estimates for others.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Dated agent/scaffold versions receive repeated runs; a logistic fit relates binary task success to human expert completion time. The source weights task families.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: A fifty-percent success horizon is a task-difficulty measure in human-time units, not autonomous uptime or a guarantee of completion.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: The inspected prose lists 97+7+66 suite tasks but separately reports 148 of 169 with human baselines and a footnote with additional tasks. No aggregate denominator is inferred from these differing scope statements. Exact reconciliation would require the task-level dataset/filters. This does not alter the metric-definition conclusion.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Reconcile the versioned task-level dataset and fitting filters before any denominator-sensitive reanalysis or forecast claim.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: 20 air–ground simulator scenarios: 12 nominal and 8 deliberately unrecoverable fault cases; one feedback replan allowed.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: Gazebo/PX4 SITL/ROS2 main comparison; separate selected hardware demonstrations.
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: LLM-only, skill-list, runtime-observation prompt and enforced runtime-observation conditions; latter two share prompt.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Dispatch validity, completed nominal tasks and behaviour on unrecoverable faults.
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Enforcement prevents observed invalid dispatch in the tested set; reported zero false dispatch has a non-zero upper confidence limit. Fault cases test refusal, not successful recovery.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: Small correlated scenario set, source confidence intervals and recent unreplicated preprint.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: Harness-specific gates, intentionally unrecoverable faults, simulator transfer and selected separate hardware examples.

REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.design_and_population: Twenty air–ground simulator scenarios: twelve nominal and eight deliberately unrecoverable faults; one feedback replan allowed. Two selected hardware demonstrations are separate.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.comparator_and_measurement: Four conditions include language-model-only, skill-list, runtime-observation prompt and runtime-observation enforcement; the latter two share prompt content.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.supported_result: The enforced gate prevents observed invalid dispatch in this harness; the fault cases mainly discriminate refusal from attempted execution, not successful recovery.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.bias_uncertainty_and_dependence: Small correlated scenario set, chosen faults, simulator/hardware gap and a recent unreplicated preprint. Zero observed failures does not mean zero failure probability; confidence bounds remain source-reported.
REQUALIFICATION_ANALYSIS.next_discriminator: Test materially new faults and physical timing/actuation conditions with an adequate baseline and protected procedure.

evidence_case_catalogue.SAMPLE: Observational study of 2,611 rubric-scored production interviews over fourteen batches for one deployed voice/video interviewing agent, with overlapping reviewers, change logs and support tickets.
evidence_case_catalogue.SETTING: One deployed interviewing-agent programme
evidence_case_catalogue.COMPARISON: Reviewer fixed effects and time/batch models distinguish rating severity from latent reliability under assignment and stability assumptions. Interview-related support tickets provide a separate correlated business outcome.
evidence_case_catalogue.MEASURES: Rating comparability, longitudinal latent-state estimates and support-ticket association
evidence_case_catalogue.OUTCOME: Reviewer composition can materially alter raw trends; the reported reviewer B contrast is about -0.792 standard deviations. The paper explicitly does not identify evaluation’s causal effect on performance.
evidence_case_catalogue.UNCERTAINTY: One production programme, nonrandom reviewer/task assignment, additive stable-severity assumptions, unlogged vendor/configuration/population changes and few temporal shifts. Illustrative return calculations omit engineering and assume uncertain attribution.
evidence_case_catalogue.VALIDITY_THREATS: One production programme, nonrandom reviewer/task assignment, additive stable-severity assumptions, unlogged vendor/configuration/population changes and few temporal shifts.
